original_question: Let a(n) be Stern's diatomic sequence, defined by a(0) = 0, a(1) = 1, a(2n) = a(n), and a(2n + 1) = a(n) + a(n + 1). For L in N_0, define Q^(L)(N) = sum_{n=2^N+1}^{2^(N+1)} a(n)^L. Proposition 1 states that there is a unique algebraic number mu_L and a constant c_L such that Q^(L)(N)/2^N is asymptotic to c_L mu_L^N. Does there exist a function p(x) - analytic, continuous of bounded variation, or more generally a distribution - such that int_0^((1+sqrt(5))/2) x^L dp(x) = mu_L for every L >= 0?
target_in_paper: Section 9, Problem 12: the paper’s open problem about whether the algebraic quantities μ_L arising from Stern-sequence block moments are themselves the Stieltjes moments of some function, preferably analytic or at least of bounded variation, or more generally of a distribution; Proposition 1 is the immediate setup that defines μ_L. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.09842))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures almost all of the paper-faithful content: the Stern diatomic sequence is defined correctly; the block-moment sums Q^(L)(N) are the right objects; μ_L is correctly tied to Proposition 1; and the actual research direction is exactly the existence of an integrator p whose moments recover μ_L, with the same regularity menu as in the paper (analytic / bounded variation / distribution). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))
missing_details: The target should be identified explicitly as Problem 12 in Section 9, not just as a question suggested by Proposition 1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))

It should be stated that μ_L is, for each fixed L, the unique algebraic number supplied by Proposition 1 via the asymptotic formula for Q^(L)(N)/2^N as N→∞. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))
The integral is a Stieltjes-moment condition with respect to p (or its distributional analogue), not an ordinary Lebesgue-density moment ∫ x^L p(x) dx. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))

The paper does not impose positivity, probability normalization, uniqueness, or absolute continuity of p; broadening to those stronger conditions would go beyond the paper. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))

The support interval [0,(1+sqrt(5))/2] should be retained as part of the question, since the paper places the moment problem on that interval rather than on an arbitrary domain. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))
refined_question: Let a(0)=0, a(1)=1, a(2n)=a(n), and a(2n+1)=a(n)+a(n+1) be Stern’s diatomic sequence, and for L,N in N_0 define Q^(L)(N)=sum_{n=2^N+1}^{2^(N+1)} a(n)^L. For each fixed L>=0, let μ_L be the unique algebraic number given by Proposition 1 such that Q^(L)(N)/2^N is asymptotic to c_L μ_L^N for some constant c_L. Does there exist a function p on [0,(1+sqrt(5))/2]—ideally analytic, or at least continuous of bounded variation, or more generally a distribution—such that its Stieltjes moments satisfy int_0^((1+sqrt(5))/2) x^L dp(x)=μ_L for every L>=0? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1609.09842))
justification: The draft is aimed at the paper’s Section 9 open problem on “interpolating the moments of the Stern’s diatomic sequence”: the abstract flags that topic, Section 9 introduces the block moments Q^(L)(N), Proposition 1 provides the algebraic numbers μ_L, and Problem 12 asks whether these numbers are moments of some function/distribution on [0,(1+sqrt(5))/2]. The rewrite therefore stays narrowly with Problem 12 and uses Proposition 1 only to define μ_L, without adding stronger assumptions not present in the paper. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.09842))
